messages.content: The Galaxy S23 Ultra I received has visible scratches and scuffs. This doesn't look refurbished to me — it looks like a used phone. I'd like a refund.

I'm sorry you're not happy with it. However, the listing clearly described the condition as 'Refurbished - Good' and itemized every cosmetic issue — the three back scuffs, the hairline screen scratch, and the S Pen wear. Did you read the full listing before purchasing?
I read the listing but 'refurbished' implies the device was restored. Listing scratches and scuffs on a 'refurbished' item is misleading. You should have listed this as 'used' not 'refurbished.'

Refurbished means it was tested, had components replaced (new battery in this case), and graded. The 'Good' condition grade means there are visible cosmetic marks, which I disclosed. This is standard industry terminology. The phone is exactly as described.
